title: Dutch court jails two men for bank helpdesk fraud caught in police decoy operation
date_note: Security.nl's page (24 November) gives no earlier day for the ruling; the date is its publication day.
geo_basis: country-level; the article does not name the court (Noord-Holland police ran the operation)
summary: Security.nl reports a police judge sentenced two men, from Rotterdam and Ridderkerk, to three months' unconditional imprisonment each for fraud committed in association. They were arrested after collecting bank cards and valuables from people who were in fact police officers, who had entered data on phishing sites. The prosecution service said the suspects had frequently been involved in bank helpdesk fraud.
plain: Two men were jailed for three months each for phone fraud on elderly people. Police posing as victims had entered details on phishing sites, and the men were arrested when they came to collect bank cards.
exec: A Dutch court convicted two men of bank helpdesk fraud after a police decoy operation, per Security.nl; an earlier case in September ended in an acquittal.

validation.note: Only Security.nl read; the court's ruling and the prosecution service's statement were not read.

review.note: Compared title, date, sentence, towns, decoy operation, OM statement against Security.nl; single source
